title: Stream recording orchestration and kernel arbitration for multi-decode stability
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Background: We observe non-deterministic failures and rare correctness divergences during multi-stream decode when the runtime records and replays GPU graphs across overlapping prefill/decode windows. Root causes include: (a) inconsistent kernel selection decisions between record and replay due to differing occupancy hints and sequence-length distributions; (b) race conditions when stream prefill epochs are misaligned and a shared kernel hint table gets transiently updated; (c) capture abandonment when a long prefill is interrupted by a high-priority short stream causing a partial recording left in an intermediate state.

Goal: Implement a minimal, low-latency orchestration layer that makes graph recording and replay robust across interleaved decodes while preserving throughput. This ticket covers design and initial implementation of a \"recording guard\" and a deterministic kernel arbitration heuristic plus the verification harness needed for rollout.

Proposed solution summary:
- Epoch-aligned recording guard: each decode stream carries an epoch token; graph recording is gated by an atomic epoch check to guarantee the prefill window used for capture matches the intended state. Recording guard is lightweight (single atomic and a small metadata compare) to avoid added latency on the fast path.
- Kernel arbitration deterministic policy: a compact ranking function (sequence-length-weighted occupancy score + model-arch fingerprint) chosen at record time and recorded as part of the graph metadata. On replay we match or fallback deterministically to the recorded kernel variant; if incompatible, we use a documented fallback kernel and increment diagnostics counters.
- Partial-capture rollback: on interrupted captures we create an explicit tombstone marker rather than leaving incomplete graph objects. Tombstones trigger safe replay fallback and scheduled background cleanup.
- Verification harness: an e2e smoke harness that replays randomized interleaved prefill/decode patterns and verifies bitwise reproducibility for supported model families, plus a probabilistic output-similarity check for non-bitwise stable code paths.

Why this approach: it limits changes to the hot path, records minimal metadata to guarantee deterministic replay decisions, and provides clear metrics/telemetry to detect regressions. We avoid heavy-weight global locking or serializing capture across streams which would reduce throughput.

Deliverables for this ticket: design doc, runtime changes (recording guard + kernel ranking + tombstone mark), replay verifier integration, CI coverage, canary plan and observability (dashboard + alerts).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Deterministic replay: under the e2e harness (5000 randomized interleavings across short/long streams), no bitwise divergences for our stable test models; failures flagged as test failures in CI.
2) Performance: p99 decode latency regression <= 3% vs baseline for mixed workload (1:4 short-to-long stream ratio), and throughput drop <= 5% measured on dedicated CI rig.
3) Capture failure rate < 0.1% in 48h canary under representative load; tombstone + fallback logic prevents client-visible failures.
4) Observability: new Grafana panels for capture_success_rate, capture_tombstone_rate, kernel_fallback_rate, and per-stream-epoch-mismatch metric implemented and surfaced.
5) Rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag and enabled for 5% of dedicated pool, with automatic rollback on >0.5% customer-impacting error rate.

risks: Increased metadata size could affect memory pressure for very small models if not compacted.
Incorrect ranking heuristics may increase kernel fallback rate leading to throughput regressions.
Edge-case models (custom ops) may be incompatible with deterministic replay; will need explicit opt-outs.
Rollback complexity if tombstones leak; requires reliable background cleanup
perf_targets: p99 latency regression <= 3% (mixed workload) - measured via perf harness
Throughput drop <= 5% for 1:4 short:long ratio workload
test_plan: Unit tests for epoch token compare logic and tombstone lifecycle
Deterministic e2e harness that replays 5k randomized interleavings overnight
CI job on dedicated hardware that runs a 1-hour mixed workload and reports p99/throughput
Canary on production-like dedicated pool with automatic metrics gating (48h)
Manual regression check: run previously failing customer trace through harness and confirm behavior
